list.name: Vivi Music 6.0.8.5_DE 1.54.21
list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.5_DE 1.54.21
**Release channel:** `beta`

### 🐛 Fixed
- [DE] **The tracks that stopped with `giving up after 3 attempts: HTTP 403 downloading audio` were being handed a URL signed by a client that cannot work on a desktop.** The user's own `~/.vivimusic/logs/20261007-205734/playback.log` shows the shape of it: `stream ready for 'Ban this guy' (network)` and then, 400 ms later, `playback error: HTTP 403 downloading audio`, three times in a row, track after track, and every failing URL carries `c=WEB_CREATOR`. That client, and `WEB_REMIX`, `TVHTML5` and `TVHTML5_SIMPLY` with it, i.e. every client flagged `useWebPoTokens`, signs a URL that googlevideo serves only when the request carries a PoToken, and a PoToken needs a WebView: the phone has one, this app does not. A web client in the chain is therefore not "a weaker fallback", it is a guaranteed 403 that eats a play attempt and makes the retry re-resolve through the same dead end, which is exactly the three attempts in the log. The chain is PoToken-free now, and `filterNot { it.useWebPoTokens }` enforces that instead of trusting the list, so a day when every free identity is refused ends with **no candidate at all**, the case the retry path already handles correctly (rotate the guest identity and resolve again) instead of playing a URL that is known to fail. **Measured with a new probe**, `./gradlew :desktop:streamResolveProbe`, which resolves real tracks and fetches the first 256 KB of every candidate with that candidate's own User-Agent: the four tracks that failed in that log, plus a fifth that played fine, each return two candidates answering `206` (`VISIONOS`, then `ANDROID_VR` 1.65.10), while the same track signed by `WEB_CREATOR` cannot even be resolved (`WEB_CREATOR returned no playable format`).
- [DE] **`VISIONOS` leads the client chain because it was measured to answer.** The old first client, `ANDROID_VR_1_43_32`, produced no URL at all for any of the five probe tracks, so every single play paid a resolution round-trip that never contributed a candidate. The PoToken-free identities the client table already defines follow it, most reliable first (`ANDROID_VR_1_65_10`, `IPADOS`, `IOS`, `ANDROID_VR_1_43_32`, `ANDROID_CREATOR`, `MWEB`, `TVHTML5_SIMPLY_EMBEDDED_PLAYER`), so a track that is flagged for one identity still plays through another. **Watch:** a play that used to end in `giving up after 3 attempts` must now end in `resolution failed, rotating guest and retrying` at worst, and `streamResolveProbe` must report a `2xx` candidate for every track it resolves.

### ✨ Added
- [DE] **The Listen Together chat window has a close button and a keyboard shortcut.** The window could only be closed from its title bar, and opened only from the room screen, so it was easy to open by accident and awkward to bring up while reading the library. The header now carries a close control for the same reason the room carries the button that opens it, and `Ctrl+Shift+C` toggles the window from anywhere in the app (plain `Ctrl+C` is copy and the combination is claimed by nothing else here). The room's Chat card writes the shortcut under the last message, because a shortcut nobody knows about is a shortcut nobody uses. **Watch:** `Ctrl+Shift+C` with a room open must open the window, and again must close it.

### 📝 Commits
- v6.0.8.5_DE-1.54.21: stop handing the player a web client URL, and let the chat window be closed from the keyboard

---
This release was built automatically from commit `83ea5ea8c3e485940ba0c9c5b0faf4e7504680ff`.

list.name: Vivi Music 6.0.8.5_DE 1.54.20
list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.5_DE 1.54.20
**Release channel:** `beta`

### 🐛 Fixed
- [DE] **The changelog emoji are drawn, in colour, on every path.** Reported as `🐛 Fixed`, `🔧 Changed` and `📝 Commits` showing *a question mark inside a rhombus* while `✨ Added` was fine, and that is exactly the shape of the bug: `markdownInline` appended one UTF-16 code unit per span, so every emoji from the supplementary plane (`U+1F000` and up, which is `🐛` `🔧` `📝` `🗑️` `📌` `🌍`) had a span boundary **in the middle of its surrogate pair**. The two halves became two layout runs and the pair stopped matching any glyph, so the renderer drew the app font's `.notdef`; `✨` (`U+2728`, one unit) had no such boundary and was drawn normally. The plain-character branch takes a whole code point now. **Measured, not assumed:** `:desktop:changelogEmojiCheck` renders the real Markdown path (`markdownInline` and `MarkdownView`) into an off-screen `ImageComposeScene` and counts ink and chromatic pixels. Before: `ink=223 colour=0` for all six (and 403/340 for `✨` on the same path). After: each emoji draws **exactly** what its own family draws (403/340, 377/0, 911/171, 372/334, 761/0, 455/381, 856/812), so no glyph-less face answers, and the seven real headings (`### 🐛 Fixed` and the rest) carry colour. Two of them (`🔧`, `🗑️`) are grey **in the Twemoji artwork itself**, which is why the check compares ink against the resolved family instead of demanding chroma.
- [DE] **The colour emoji font is bundled, COLRv0, and was measured before it was chosen.** The previous `NotoColorEmoji.ttf` was a 165 KB COLR/CPAL subset whose glyphs this renderer painted as **nothing at all** (0 ink), which is why the code then routed those codepoints to the monochrome face and the changelog had no colour anywhere. Three candidates were rasterised through Skiko with a standalone probe: the old subset (0 ink for every emoji), the full Noto Color Emoji (25 MB, COLRv1: 0 ink for every emoji, rejected), and **Twemoji Mozilla 0.7.0** (1.47 MB, COLRv0: paints colour, e.g. `✨` 1320 ink / 1265 chromatic). Twemoji is what ships now (`fonts/TwemojiColorEmoji.ttf`), `NotoEmoji.ttf` stays as the monochrome fallback for the codepoints the colour face lacks, and the coverage list is generated from the fonts' own `cmap` by `scripts/build_desktop_emoji_coverage.py` (`--check` fails on a stale list). **Watch:** `:desktop:changelogEmojiCheck` must end with `OK: every changelog emoji is drawn, in colour, on every path`.
- [DE] **Listen Together no longer crashes with a duplicate `LazyColumn` key.** The user's own dump says it: `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Key "f4678da9-…" was already used. If you are using LazyColumn/Row please make sure you provide a unique key for each item.` (`~/.vivimusic/logs/20261007-211837/crash_*.log`). Three lists were keyed by an identity they did not guarantee: `USER_JOINED` appended a second row for a user who joined twice, `JOIN_REQUEST` and `SUGGESTION_RECEIVED` appended a repeat, and the chat list is keyed by `timestamp-userId-message`, so the same line arriving twice was a duplicate key. All three now replace their entry instead of appending a second one (the chat drops an identical message from the same author in the same millisecond, which is indistinguishable anyway), the state a `RECONNECTED` message brings in is deduplicated, and the screen deduplicates by key a second time before drawing, because a duplicate key is a crash and not a cosmetic problem. The second dump, `layout state is not idle before measure starts` while a window was being disposed, is Compose's own re-entrant measure and the state the first crash left the app in, not a second bug.
- [DE] **Logs older than seven days are deleted automatically.** `~/.vivimusic/logs/<session>/` gained one folder per launch and nothing ever removed them, so the tree grew without a bound. Startup now deletes the session folders older than seven days **and** any loose `.log` file in `~/.vivimusic/` (`actions.log`, `login-debug.log`, `crash.log`; every crash dump is also written inside the session it happened in, so a week of crash evidence stays). The rule is a pure function, checked by `:desktop:localDataMaintenanceCheck` against files in a temporary directory: an eight day old session folder and `.log` are selected, three day old ones are not, the session being written never is, and **no data file ever is**. That check caught the first version of the rule, which trusted its caller to have filtered the list to `.log` files, which is exactly how `settings.json` gets deleted by a future edit.

### ✨ Added
- [DE] **Storage is a card screen now, ported from mobile.** Two cards in the shape the rest of the settings use: the cache (its size, and the button that clears it) and the downloaded installers (their size, and the button that deletes them), with the privacy note that says these files are local. The mobile screen's two sliders are deliberately **not** ported: they set an image-cache and a song-cache ceiling that only exist on Android, so on the desktop they would be controls wired to nothing. The installer card counts and deletes the same set as the Updates counter, so the number and the button cannot disagree.
- [DE] **The first-run screen is rebuilt from scratch, on the mobile welcome flow.** Three steps: **Welcome** (logo, title, the DE developer, the language picker), **Community** (star the repository, join `t.me/vivimusicde`, support via UPI, buy the developer a coffee) and **Discover the desktop features** (the now-playing widget, the media keys, the tray menu, i.e. what the phone cannot show). The language picker is a card that opens a **searchable** list of the 48 shipped languages, matching the native name and the code, because picking one out of 48 rows was the weak part of the screen this replaces. The two support links are the **mobile developer's own** (`upi://pay?pa=vividhpashokan@axl&pn=Vividh P Ashokan` and `https://ko-fi.com/vividhpashokan`), as the mobile welcome screen has them. It runs only on a fresh install (no language chosen yet) and is not re-openable from Settings, and it stays up until the user finishes it even though its first step already saves the language. **Watch:** `:desktop:firstRunRenderCheck` renders it off screen at 600x480, 1024x768 and 1600x900 and fails on a crash or on a screen that paints nothing.
- [DE] **The Listen Together chat has a window of its own, with replies and notifications.** The conversation used to be a list and a text field at the bottom of the room screen, which is the wrong shape twice over: it was clipped to the room's own scroll, and it disappeared the moment the user left the screen while the room kept playing. It is a real window now (`ListenTogetherChatWindow.kt`, emitted beside the live-log window so it outlives the room screen), drawn the way a chat is expected to look: own messages right-aligned on the accent colour, everyone else's left on a neutral surface with the author above the bubble, a **date separator when the day changes** (formatted in the app language's own locale, so it needs no string in each of the 52 languages), the text selectable through the app-wide Material 3 context menu, and a reply button that appears on hover. Replying shows the quoted message above the composer and sends it in the same `reply_to` field the Android client uses, so a quote written here arrives as a quote on the phone and the other way round; `Enter` sends and `Shift+Enter` starts a new line. A message from another user while the window is closed is a **notification**, dispatched through the same `DesktopNotifier` as every other notice, which means it follows the notification-type setting (native toast or in-app banner) and is recorded in the notification history, and it raises the unread badge on the room's Chat card. **Measured:** the conversation is rendered off screen by `:desktop:chatWindowRenderCheck` (a `Window` needs a display, so the list itself was split out as `ListenTogetherChatList`), which reports `empty ink=635`, `messages (no quote) ink=60948` and `quoted ink=96972` and ends with `OK: the chat list draws, and a quoted reply draws more than the same message without it`; the quote drawing **more** than the same conversation without it is what proves it reaches the screen. **Watch:** with a room open and the window closed, a message from another user raises a notification in whichever mode the settings select; the room's Chat card shows the last line and the unread count.
- [DE] **Five strings were added to the localization tables**, authored in `scripts/desktop_extra_translations_94.py` and `scripts/desktop_extra_translations_95.py` and present in all 52 languages: the first-run screen's two support links (`support_upi`, `support_buy_me_a_coffee`) and the chat window's three (`lt_no_messages`, `lt_reply`, `lt_send_message`). The support links are BRAND names, identical in every language on purpose, which is why the audit's `BRAND_KEYS` lists them next to `telegram_channel`. **Watch:** the audit reports 52 languages, 827 English keys, 0 missing or leaking.

### 🔧 Changed
- [DE] **The window can be moved from anywhere the interface does not use.** Only the Spotify header had a drag area, so with that header hidden, and on every non-Spotify screen, the frameless window could not be moved at all. The whole window is a drag surface now, emitted **behind** the interface as the first child of the root box. Behind is the point: `WindowDraggableArea` starts moving the window on the pointer **down** and never consumes the event (both verified in the shipped bytecode), so a surface in front would nudge the window on every button click in the app. That Compose stops hit testing at the frontmost layer, so a button keeps its own clicks and the surface only sees the empty parts of the window, is not assumed either: `:desktop:framelessHitTestCheck` renders both stacks off screen and counts which layer received the press.
- [DE] **A carousel arrow exists only while its own direction can scroll.** The arrows were drawn as soon as the row could move either way, with the dead one faded to 35 percent; a row scrolled to its end kept a ghost at the right and one at its start kept a ghost at the left. Each arrow is now drawn under its own `canScrollBackward` / `canScrollForward`, and a row that fits has neither.
- [DE] **The update counter counts installs, not downloads.** An installer that has been downloaded but not run yet is the installer for the **next** version, so counting it claimed an install that had not happened. The counter, and the "delete installers" button, now work on the installers whose file name carries the version the app is currently running (`VIVIMusic-6.0.8.5_DE-1.54.20-setup.exe`), and a pending update's installer is never deleted from under the user, since the button beside it is what runs it. Once the update is actually installed the app comes up as that version and the file counts from then on.
- [DE] **Content language and content region are cards.** They were two loose buttons under two loose headings; they are now the same card shape as every other setting (through the shared `M3SettingsDropdownCard`), with the current choice on the row's trailing side and the list inline, and `system_default` first because a blank code is what `resolveYouTubeLocale` treats as "follow".
- [DE] **Material 3 Expressive, in the parts this app can reach.** The library's own `MaterialExpressiveTheme` and the flag it sets are `internal` in the Compose 1.8.2 this app compiles against (checked against the shipped bytecode: calling it is a compile error), and `ExpressiveNavigationBar` is a phone bottom bar, which this app has no use for. So the expressive pass is where the app owns the decision: the shape scale is 8/12/16/20/28 dp instead of 4/8/12/16/28, the tween motion uses the expressive emphasized curve instead of `FastOutSlowInEasing` (the panels already used an expressive spring), and the settings groups are cards with tonal icon containers.

### 📝 Commits
- v6.0.8.5_DE-1.54.20: colour emoji, a draggable window, cards, a rebuilt first run and a chat window

---
This release was built automatically from commit `f3a56f8c498dd9ed75b12635ab1b1e6fad484b7a`.

list.name: Vivi Music 6.0.8.5_DE 1.54.19
list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.5_DE 1.54.19
**Release channel:** `beta`

### 🐛 Fixed
- [DE] **The uninstaller no longer dies with `Unknown custom message name "UninstalledAll"`.** Measured against Inno Setup 7.1.0 itself: `UninstalledAll` ("%1 was successfully removed from your computer.") lives in Inno's own `[Messages]` table, while `{cm:...}` reaches `[CustomMessages]` only, so the closing box of the uninstaller raised `Runtime error ... Internal error: Unknown custom message name "UninstalledAll" in "cm" constant.` (the report, verbatim) before it could be built. The sentence is read the way a standard message has to be read, `FmtMessage(SetupMessage(msgUninstalledAll), ['VIVI Music DE'])`, which also keeps it in the language the user ran the setup in. **Verified end to end on this machine:** a probe installer using the old lookup reproduced the exact error and never reached its own last line; with the fix the same uninstaller resolved the sentence ("Probe was successfully removed from your computer."), logged `Uninstallation process succeeded` and exited 0. The full `installer/windows/VIVIMusic.iss` compiles with ISCC 7.1.0.
- [DE] **The Start Menu shows one name: VIVI Music DE.** Two names existed because two installers disagreed: jpackage's `menuGroup` said `VIVI Music` (that is what the `.msi`/`.exe` image of the app creates) while the Inno Setup script said `VIVI Music DE`, and Inno reuses the group name recorded by the previous install of the same AppId (`UsePreviousGroup`, on by default) even with the group page hidden, so an upgrade kept whichever name was there first. `menuGroup` is `VIVI Music DE` now, the script says `UsePreviousGroup=no`, and a leftover `VIVI Music` folder from an earlier installer is removed after the files are in place. **Constraint:** the old folder is only touched when it really holds this app's shortcut (`VIVIMusic.lnk` / `VIVI Music.lnk`), and every removal is written to the install log, so a folder that is not ours stays where it is.
- [DE] **The sidebar no longer shows two "Liked Songs".** The extra row was the Spotify import's playlist: it was written as a local *Liked Songs* even when it matched nothing (0 tracks), right next to the account's own *Liked Music*, which is YouTube's name for the same idea, so the list read as the same thing twice. Importing Liked Songs now **likes the matched tracks on the account** when a session is signed in (`YouTube.likeVideo`), so they join the real liked list on YouTube Music and reach every other device; the tracks the account will not take are kept in a local *Liked Songs (Spotify)* playlist so a partial run loses nothing, and a run that liked everything retires that playlist. With no session the whole match set goes to that same local playlist, named after its source. An import that matched nothing writes nothing at all, and an empty imported playlist an earlier build left behind is retired at startup. **Watch:** `spotify.log` ends the import with `liked on YouTube Music`, and the sidebar lists one liked list.
- [DE] **And an imported playlist is never pushed to YouTube Music any more.** `PlaylistSync.uploadMissing` sent every local playlist without an account id, which included the `SPOT...` rows an import owns and would have created a playlist on the account for each one, exactly the side effect the import screen promises never to have. Only the *liked songs* of an import reach the account now, and they reach it as likes. **Watch:** `playlists.log` names the imported lists it keeps local on purpose.
- [DE] **"Episodes for Later" is empty because YouTube says it is empty.** Measured with the account's own session before touching anything: browsing `VLSE` answers `secondSubtitle: 0 episodes, 0 seconds` and the shelf carries `No episodes added yet. Save episodes to this playlist to create your podcast listening queue.`, so the screen was showing the truth and the header was not losing rows. What it did do was draw nothing under **Play all** / **Shuffle all**, which looks like a broken screen; an account playlist with no tracks now says it is empty (the string the local playlist screen already uses, translated in all 52 languages) and the two buttons are only drawn when there is something to play.
- [DE] **The account's own playlist names follow the app language, not Windows'.** The sidebar listed `Musica che ti piace` and `Puntate per dopo` in an English UI: a blank "content language" fell back to the OS locale, which is the language of Windows and not the one the user picked in the app. Blank now follows the app language, an explicit *Content language* still wins, and changing the app language reaches the client at once instead of at the next restart.
- [DE] **The embedded sign-in sends the whole session, and a retry after a failure starts from an empty cookie store (issue #101).** Two changes, both from the same measurement. The captured header used to be the cookie handler's *scoped* answer plus a ten-name whitelist, and the user's own `~/.vivimusic/login-debug.log` shows what that costs: `scoped=1` (one cookie) while the store held 28 for the two sign-in domains, so every cookie outside the whitelist was dropped silently, including `LOGIN_INFO`, whose absence answers `401` and is reported as `E1033 the captured session has no LOGIN_INFO cookie` while the same cookies pasted by hand work. The header is now the scoped answer plus **every** cookie of the store for those domains, critical ones first, which is what a browser sends. And the second half of the report ("I clear the cache and it works"): **Sign in with Google** after a failed attempt drops the YouTube/Google cookies before the window loads (`LoginWebView.clearSession`), so a stale half-session can no longer poison the next capture. **Watch:** `login-debug.log` now logs `session header: N cookie(s) sent` and, after a failure, `fresh sign-in: dropped N of M YouTube/Google cookie(s)`.

### ✨ Added
- [DE] **The licence is readable inside the app, and it is loaded live.** About → Licence used to open the repository in a browser; it now opens a screen of its own that shows the full text (the GPL with the special exception for the musixmatch module). Like the contributor list, the text is fetched from the repository every time the screen opens (`LICENSE` on `vivi-music-de`, raw.githubusercontent.com) with the copy bundled in the app as the offline fallback, so a change to the licence is visible without an update. The repository entry stays at the bottom for whoever wants the file's own page.

### 🔧 Changed
- [DE] **The error dialogs now say where the error is written down.** Every error VIVI shows carries a code (`E1033`, `1009`, `SPOT-005`), and a code on its own explains nothing: both the crash dialog and the in-app error box now carry the pointer to `ERRORS.md` in the repository and to the searchable errors page (`https://piboh.github.io/vivi-music-de/errors.html`, also a click away in the dialog), and the login screen says the same under a failed sign-in.
- [DE] **The YouTube sign-in window's hints are one compact line now.** The three numbered steps were three full-width rows on their own light bar, which pushed the page itself down by a fifth of the window before it had even loaded. They are the same three sentences in a single 11.5px line, with the bar's padding cut to a strip, so the hint reads as a hint and the page gets the room.

### 📝 Commits
- v6.0.8.5_DE-1.54.19: fix the uninstaller, the double Liked Songs and the missing LOGIN_INFO
- contributors update
- contributors update
- github's contribuors update
- fix: keep the single-instance lock when a heap restart fails

---
This release was built automatically from commit `cdd770d8ab08c392bf20b30852f5849717e41e2e`.

list.name: Vivi Music 6.0.8.5_DE 1.54.18
list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.5_DE 1.54.18
**Release channel:** `beta`

### 🐛 Fixed
- [DE] **The Spotify sign-in window captures the cookies now, and that is what made the import look broken.** The cookie walk returns nothing usable because of one return value: in JCEF `CefCookieVisitor.visit` returns *keep visiting*, and the window returned `false`, which ends the walk after the very first cookie. That first cookie is almost never `sp_dc`, so every capture came back empty and the screen stayed on "Not connected to Spotify" while the sign-in itself had worked - exactly what the report said, and what `spotify.log` showed (the pages loaded, no `captured sp_dc` line ever followed). **Verified on JCEF 152.0.6 with a standalone probe against the same CEF build:** with `false` a visit of a five-cookie store delivers one cookie (`count=0 total=5`, then nothing); with `true` it delivers all five in milliseconds and deletes none. **Also verified there:** the visit must NOT be submitted from the AWT event thread - CEF dispatches the visitor callbacks on that same thread, so an event-thread visit waited three seconds and delivered zero callbacks, which is why the walk stays on the window's own thread. **Watch:** with the blocked-Google message gone the sign-in must also end by itself: `spotify.log` has to show `JCEF cookie visit returned N cookie(s): …` and then `JCEF sign-in captured sp_dc`.
- [DE] **The sign-in window no longer claims Google blocked it while the user is typing on Spotify's own form.** `onAddressChange` fires for every frame, and Spotify's sign-in page embeds Google's script, whose `accounts.google.com` iframe was enough to replace the status line and reveal *Retry* and *Open it in your browser* over a page that was working. Only the main frame is read now.
- [DE] **A language in place of another: two Developer options rows were labelled with a raw setting name.** `detailed_playback_logging` and `detailed_startup_logs` hold the literal text `DetailedPlaybackLogging` and `DetailedStartupLogs` in **all 52 languages**, so those two switches were introduced by an identifier no user should ever read. The rows show the description that was already translated everywhere. **Watch:** the audit's new cross-language checks (below) must stay clean.
- [DE] **The JVM heap actually changes now, and the app says so.** Choosing a size looked like a no-op for two reasons. The restart never happened: the code looked for a `java` launcher inside the bundled runtime, and a jpackage image does not ship one (`runtime/bin` on the installed 1.54.17 image has `java.dll` and no `java.exe`), so it gave up silently; the launcher's own `.cfg`, which holds `-Xmx2g`, sits under `Program Files` and cannot be rewritten either. What the launcher does honour is `_JAVA_OPTIONS`, and it is applied after the `.cfg`, so it replaces that `-Xmx`. **Verified against the installed image before writing this:** `VIVIMusic.exe` started with `_JAVA_OPTIONS=-Xmx3072m` came up with a maximum heap of 3221225472 bytes instead of the image's 2 GB. The restart is also watched now - if the new process exits at once, the app stays up and `app.log` records the exit code - and every decision is logged (`jvm heap: …`), so a heap that does not take effect can no longer be a silent no-op. **Verified:** the same probe on the installed runtime confirms the image's classpath resolves `com.music.vivi.desktop.MainKt`. **Constraint:** a launch from the Start Menu has no variable set, so it comes up on the image's 2 GB and the app corrects itself a moment later through the same path; that is also what makes a size chosen while the app was closed take effect.

### ✨ Added
- [DE] **The translation audit also looks for a language standing in another language's place.** Three checks were added to `scripts/audit_desktop_localization.py`: the language code must be served by its own table (`"zh-rCN"` by `strings_zh_rCN`, not by a neighbour's), the picker must name each code with that language's own endonym ("Polski" for `pl`), and a value may not carry a letter that belongs to another language's alphabet (`ß`, `ł`, `ő`, `đ`, `õ`, `ñ` and the rest, with the letters several languages share kept out of the comparison so a language is never reported against its own text). **Result on this tree:** 52 languages, 822 English keys, 0 missing or leaking, 0 wrong-script, 0 foreign letters, and the two raw identifiers above found and fixed. The three remaining `English text left` entries are `jvm_memory_default` in Filipino, Indonesian and `in`, where "Default" is the local word.

### 🔧 Changed
- [DE] **The heap preparation bar moved to the screen that opened the sign-in window.** It used to sit in the window's own header, next to the status and the ways out, which is not where the user is looking when a first run spends a while downloading and unpacking Chromium. It is now drawn under **Sign in to Spotify** on the import screen, with the percentage, and it is not shown at all once the page is up.
- [DE] **The sign-in window's header is one row again:** a spinner and the status, with *Retry* and *Open it in your browser* appearing in that same row only after Google refuses its page. Both are flat, borderless and in the accent the other sign-in window's links use, so the two windows read as the same program; the long blocked sentence is carried in full in the row's tooltip instead of being clipped.
- [DE] **Turn off developer options is a switch now**, the way Android's own developer-options screen turns them off, instead of a row that opens a question. It sits first and still asks once, because turning it off resets every option below.
- [DE] **The account row at the bottom left opens the Account screen directly.** The row *is* the account (name and avatar), so landing on the general settings list meant clicking the same thing twice; the gear in the rail is the way to that list. The row stays highlighted on both screens.
- [DE] **The expressive player's panel can no longer be closed by accident.** The queue / lyrics / history tabs used to toggle the panel off, and they took the tab strip down with them: once the panel was closed there was no control left to open it again, so the only way back was to relaunch the app. The tabs are selectors now, the panel and its strip are always there, and the stored tab is restored on the section the user left it on (a stored "closed" from an older build opens on the queue). The player itself still closes with the chevron at the top left.

### 📝 Commits
- v6.0.8.5_DE-1.54.18: capture the Spotify cookies, and make the JVM heap change

---
This release was built automatically from commit `2dab3978cc1a785c73fc9d57108f790136520fa8`.

list.name: Vivi Music 6.0.8.5_DE 1.54.17
list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.5_DE 1.54.17
**Release channel:** `beta`

### 🐛 Fixed
- [DE] **The main window remembers its size and position again.** The placement was saved correctly (`1207x1017@621,58` in `settings.json`) but the restore clamped it into the rectangle `maximumWindowBounds` reports before the window is shown, and that rectangle came back bogus (`526x478@621,597`): the clamp then both shrank and moved a perfectly valid placement, and every logged session opened at exactly that size. The saved floating bounds are clamped only against a screen the environment reports as *real* (at least 800x600) now; a bogus or smaller one is ignored and the saved size is used as it is. The restore is also re-asserted once the window is actually shown, and the decision is logged (`restore: saved=… usable=… applied=…` in `window.log`) so the next session shows exactly what was applied.
- [DE] **Quitting from the tray keeps the window's placement too.** The tray's Quit called `exitApplication` directly and never ran the close request that persists the geometry, so a session ended from the tray reopened at the previous size and position. Both exit paths persist it now, and a minimized window's parked bounds (`-32000,-32000 160x28`) are no longer written, which would otherwise be restored as the window's placement.
